articles.summary: Xilinx researchers in Beijing re-implement a hardware-friendly quantization baseline following references [19, 21], where [19] is TQT, and apply their bin regularization on top of TQT. Their Table 9 reports TQT, TQT+L2 and TQT+BR results for 4-bit MobileNetV2. Employer-linked: the authors list Xilinx Inc.
articles.research_connection: Builds bin regularization on the TQT baseline: Table 9 reports 63.8% top-1 for TQT and 67.5% for TQT+BR on 4-bit MobileNetV2, which the text describes as +3.7% over TQT.

articles.research_connection: States "For the quantization strategy, a power-of-two scale quantizer with training quantization threshold (TQT) was used [50]" in the AMD DPU quantization-aware training (p. 9).

articles.research_connection: States that ITBWN uses TQT INT8 quantization for its activations (p. 3) and labels its binary, ternary and INT8 configurations by their use of TQT (p. 4).

articles.research_connection: States that the TQT method is used to transform the pruned FP32 model into a 4-bit fixed-point model during training (p. 4); the quantized model is deployed on the FPGA.

articles.summary: The Alan Turing Institute researchers deploy a YOLOv8-based SAR vessel detector on an AMD/Xilinx Kria KV260 FPGA. They quantize it to INT8 with the Vitis AI Quantizer using power-of-two scaling and quantization-aware training attributed to TQT, train the quantizer parameters and deploy the resulting QAT models.
articles.research_connection: Cites TQT [35] for its power-of-two QAT with a straight-through estimator (p. 5), retrains with a tuned quantizer parameter learning rate and reports the deployed FPGA QAT models in Table 4 (p. 11). TQT is cited rather than named, and was used through the AMD/Xilinx Vitis AI toolchain.
